hints.title: Recursive Subtree Summation
hints.text: The sum of any subtree equals the root value plus the total sums of its left and right child subtrees.

hints.title: Post-Order Bottom-Up Traversal
hints.text: Calculate subtree totals bottom-up and record each sum in a frequency counter map.

hints.title: Peak Frequency Extraction
hints.text: Traverse post-order to compute each node sum. Increment frequency in counts map. After completing the tree visit, find the maximum count and return all keys matching that maximum.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import List, Optional

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right

class Solution:
    def findFrequentTreeSum(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> List[int]:
        counts = defaultdict(int)

        def dfs(node: Optional[TreeNode]) -> int:
            if not node:
                return 0
            total = node.val + dfs(node.left) + dfs(node.right)
            counts[total] += 1
            return total

        dfs(root)
        max_freq = max(counts.values())
        return [s for s, c in counts.items() if c == max_freq]
```

variables: N: number of nodes in tree
complexity.notes: Post-order traversal visiting each node once with hash map tallying.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recomputing sums repeatedly from top to bottom incurs quadratic O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Bottom-up aggregation caches child subtree sums in recursion returns.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use post-order traversal to compute subtree sums in O(N) linear time.
